verses.zh: 「赎愆祭的条例乃是如此：这祭是至圣的。
verses.en: “‘This is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy.

verses.zh: 人在那里宰燔祭牲，也要在那里宰赎愆祭牲；其血，祭司要洒在坛的周围。
verses.en: In the place where they slaughter the burnt offering they must slaughter the guilt offering, and the officiating priest[NOTE:1] must splash[NOTE:2] the blood against the altar’s sides.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the officiating priest) has been specified in the translation for clarity. This priest was responsible for any actions involving direct contact with the altar (e.g., the splashing of the blood).
See the note on Lev 1:5.

verses.zh: 又要将肥尾巴和盖脏的脂油，
verses.en: Then the one making the offering[NOTE:1] must present all its fat: the fatty tail, the fat covering the entrails,
notes: Heb “then he.” This pronoun refers to the offerer, who was responsible for slaughtering the animal. Contrast v. 2 above and v. 5 below.

verses.zh: 两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，并肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下。
verses.en: the two kidneys and the fat on their sinews, and the protruding lobe on the liver (which he must remove along with the kidneys).[NOTE:1]
notes: See the notes on Lev 3:3-4.

verses.zh: 祭司要在坛上焚烧，为献给耶和华的火祭，是赎愆祭。
verses.en: Then the priest must offer them up in smoke on the altar[NOTE:1] as a gift to the Lord. It is a guilt offering.
notes: See the note on Lev 1:9 above.

verses.zh: 祭司中的男丁都可以吃这祭物；要在圣处吃，是至圣的。
verses.en: Any male among the priests may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “holiness of holinesses [or holy of holies] it is”; NAB “most sacred”; TEV “very holy.”

verses.zh: 赎罪祭怎样，赎愆祭也是怎样，两个祭是一个条例。献赎愆祭赎罪的祭司要得这祭物。
verses.en: The law is the same for the sin offering and the guilt offering;[NOTE:1] it belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
notes: Heb “like the sin offering like the guilt offering, one law to them.”

verses.zh: 献燔祭的祭司，无论为谁奉献，要亲自得他所献那燔祭牲的皮。
verses.en: “‘As for the priest who presents someone’s burnt offering, the hide of that burnt offering which he presented belongs to him.

verses.zh: 凡在炉中烤的素祭和煎盘中做的，并铁鏊上做的，都要归那献祭的祭司。
verses.en: Every grain offering which is baked in the oven or[NOTE:1] made in the pan[NOTE:2] or on the griddle belongs to the priest who presented it.
notes: Heb “and” rather than “or” (cf. also the next “or”).
Heb “and all made in the pan”; cf. KJV “fryingpan”; NAB “deep-fried in a pot.”

verses.zh: 凡素祭，无论是油调和的是干的，都要归亚伦的子孙，大家均分。」
verses.en: Every grain offering, whether mixed with olive oil or dry, belongs to all the sons of Aaron, each one alike.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “a man like his brother.”

verses.zh: 「人献与耶和华平安祭的条例乃是这样：
verses.en: “‘This is the law of the peace-offering sacrifice which he[NOTE:1] is to present to the Lord.
notes: This “he” pronoun refers to the offerer. Smr and LXX have plural “they.”

verses.zh: 他若为感谢献上，就要用调油的无酵饼和抹油的无酵薄饼，并用油调匀细面做的饼，与感谢祭一同献上。
verses.en: If he presents it on account of thanksgiving,[NOTE:1] along with the thank-offering sacrifice he must present unleavened loaves mixed with olive oil, unleavened wafers smeared with olive oil,[NOTE:2] and well-soaked,[NOTE:3] ring-shaped loaves made of choice wheat flour[NOTE:4] mixed with olive oil.
notes: Or “for a thank offering.”
See the notes on Lev 2:4.
See the note on Lev 6:21 [6:14 HT].
Heb “choice wheat flour well-soaked ring-shaped loaves.” See the note on Lev 2:1.

verses.zh: 要用有酵的饼和为感谢献的平安祭，与供物一同献上。
verses.en: He must present this grain offering[NOTE:1] in addition to ring-shaped loaves of leavened bread which regularly accompany[NOTE:2] the sacrifice of his thanksgiving peace offering.
notes: The rendering “this [grain] offering” is more literally “his offering,” but it refers to the series of grain offerings listed just previously in v. 12.

The words “which regularly accompany” are not in the Hebrew text, but are supplied for clarity.sn The translation “[which regularly accompany]…” is based on the practice of bringing bread (and wine) to eat with the portions of the peace-offering meat eaten by the priests and worshipers (see v. 14 and Num 15:1-13). This was in addition to the memorial portion of the unleavened bread that was offered to the Lord on the altar (cf. Lev 2:2, 9, and the note on 7:12).

verses.zh: 从各样的供物中，他要把一个饼献给耶和华为举祭，是要归给洒平安祭牲血的祭司。
verses.en: He must present one of each kind of grain offering[NOTE:1] as a contribution offering[NOTE:2] to the Lord; it belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the peace offering.
notes: Here the Hebrew text reads “offering” (קָרְבָּן, qorban), not “grain offering” (מִנְחָה, minkhah), but in this context the term refers once again to the list in 7:12.

The term rendered “contribution offering” is תְּרוּמָה (terumah), which generally refers to that which is set aside from the offerings to the Lord as prebends for the officiating priests (cf. esp. Lev 7:28-34 and R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 4:335-37). Cf. TEV “as a special contribution.”

verses.zh: 为感谢献平安祭牲的肉，要在献的日子吃，一点不可留到早晨。
verses.en: The meat of his[NOTE:1] thanksgiving peace offering must be eaten on the day of his offering; he must not set any of it aside until morning.
notes: In the verse “his” refers to the offerer.

verses.zh: 若所献的是为还愿，或是甘心献的，必在献祭的日子吃，所剩下的第二天也可以吃。
verses.en: “‘If his offering is a votive or freewill sacrifice,[NOTE:1] it may be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, and also the leftovers from it may be eaten on the next day,[NOTE:2]
notes: For the distinction between votive and freewill offerings see the note on Lev 22:23 and the literature cited there.
Heb “and on the next day and the left over from it shall be eaten.”

verses.zh: 但所剩下的祭肉，到第三天要用火焚烧；
verses.en: but the leftovers from the meat of the sacrifice must be burned up in the fire[NOTE:1] on the third day.
notes: Heb “burned with fire,” an expression which is sometimes redundant in English, but here means “burned up,” “burned up entirely” (likewise in v. 19).

verses.zh: 第三天若吃了平安祭的肉，这祭必不蒙悦纳，人所献的也不算为祭，反为可憎嫌的，吃这祭肉的，就必担当他的罪孽。
verses.en: If some of the meat of his peace-offering sacrifice is ever eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted; it will not be accounted to the one who presented it since it is spoiled,[NOTE:1] and the person who eats from it will bear his punishment for iniquity.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “desecrated,” or “defiled,” or “forbidden.” For this difficult term see J. Milgrom, Leviticus (AB), 1:422. Cf. NIV “it has become impure”; NCV “it will become unclean”; NLT “will be contaminated.”
Heb “his iniquity he shall bear” (cf. Lev 5:1); NIV “will be held responsible”; NRSV “shall incur guilt”; TEV “will suffer the consequences.”

verses.zh: 「挨了污秽物的肉就不可吃，要用火焚烧。至于平安祭的肉，凡洁净的人都要吃；
verses.en: The meat which touches anything ceremonially unclean[NOTE:1] must not be eaten; it must be burned up in the fire. As for ceremonially clean meat,[NOTE:2] everyone who is ceremonially clean may eat the meat.
notes: The word “ceremonially” has been supplied in the translation both here and in the following sentence to clarify that the uncleanness involved is ritual or ceremonial in nature.
The Hebrew has simply “the flesh,” but this certainly refers to “clean” flesh in contrast to the unclean flesh in the first half of the verse.

verses.zh: 只是献与耶和华平安祭的肉，人若不洁净而吃了，这人必从民中剪除。
verses.en: The person who eats meat from the peace-offering sacrifice which belongs to the Lord while that person’s uncleanness persists[NOTE:1] will be cut off from his people.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and his unclean condition is on him.”

The exact meaning of this penalty clause is not certain. It could mean that he will be executed, whether by God or by man, he will be excommunicated from sanctuary worship and/or community benefits (cf. TEV, CEV), or his line will be terminated by God (i.e., extirpation), etc. See J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 100; J. Milgrom, Leviticus (AB), 1:457-60; and B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 241-42 for further discussion.

verses.zh: 有人摸了甚么不洁净的物，或是人的不洁净，或是不洁净的牲畜，或是不洁可憎之物，吃了献与耶和华平安祭的肉，这人必从民中剪除。」
verses.en: When a person touches anything unclean (whether human uncleanness, or an unclean animal, or an unclean detestable creature)[NOTE:1] and eats some of the meat of the peace-offering sacrifice which belongs to the Lord, that person will be cut off from his people.’”[NOTE:2]
notes: For these categories of unclean animals see Lev 11.
For the interpretation of this last clause see the note on Lev 7:20.

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on Lev 6:8 [6:1 HT] above.

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：牛的脂油、绵羊的脂油、山羊的脂油，你们都不可吃。
verses.en: “Tell the Israelites, ‘You must not eat any fat of an ox, sheep, or goat.

verses.zh: 自死的和被野兽撕裂的，那脂油可以做别的使用，只是你们万不可吃。
verses.en: Moreover, the fat of an animal that has died of natural causes[NOTE:1] and the fat of an animal torn by beasts may be used for any other purpose,[NOTE:2] but you must certainly never eat it.
notes: Heb “carcass,” referring to the carcass of an animal that has died on its own, not the carcass of an animal slaughtered for sacrifice or killed by wild beasts. This has been clarified in the translation by supplying the phrase “of natural causes”; cf. NAB, TEV “that has died a natural death.”
Heb “shall be used for any work”; cf. NIV, NLT “may be used for any other purpose.”

verses.zh: 无论何人吃了献给耶和华当火祭牲畜的脂油，那人必从民中剪除。
verses.en: If anyone eats fat from the animal from which he presents a gift to the Lord, that person will be cut off from his people.[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on Lev 7:20.

verses.zh: 在你们一切的住处，无论是雀鸟的血是野兽的血，你们都不可吃。
verses.en: And you must not eat any blood of the birds or of the domesticated land animals in any of the places where you live.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and any blood you must not eat in any of your dwelling places, to the bird and to the animal.”

verses.zh: 无论是谁吃血，那人必从民中剪除。」
verses.en: Any person who eats any blood—that person will be cut off from his people.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on Lev 7:20.

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on Lev 6:8 [6:1 HT].

verses.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：献平安祭给耶和华的，要从平安祭中取些来奉给耶和华。
verses.en: “Tell the Israelites, ‘The one who presents his peace-offering sacrifice to the Lord must bring part of his offering to the Lord as his sacrifice.

verses.zh: 他亲手献给耶和华的火祭，就是脂油和胸，要带来，好把胸在耶和华面前作摇祭，摇一摇。
verses.en: With his own hands he must bring the Lord’s gifts. He must bring the fat with the breast[NOTE:1] to wave the breast as a wave offering before the Lord,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “on the breast.”

Heb “the breast to wave it, a wave offering before the Lord.” Other possible translations are “to elevate the breast [as] an elevation offering before the Lord” (cf. NRSV) or “to present the breast [as] a presentation offering before the Lord.” See J. E. Hartley, Leviticus (WBC), 91, J. Milgrom, Leviticus (AB), 1:430-31, 461-72, and R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 3:63-67. tc Many Hebrew mss and some versions (esp. the LXX) limit the offerings in the last part of this verse to the fat portions, specifically, the fat and the fat lobe of the liver (see the BHS footnote). The verse is somewhat awkward in Hebrew but nevertheless correct.

verses.zh: 祭司要把脂油在坛上焚烧，但胸要归亚伦和他的子孙。
verses.en: and the priest must offer the fat up in smoke on the altar, but the breast will belong to Aaron and his sons.

verses.zh: 你们要从平安祭中把右腿作举祭，奉给祭司。
verses.en: The right thigh you must give as a contribution offering[NOTE:1] to the priest from your peace-offering sacrifice.
notes: Older English versions (e.g., KJV, ASV) translate this Hebrew term (תְּרוּמָה, terumah) “heave offering,” derived from the idea of “to raise, to lift” found in the verbal root (cf. NAB “a raised offering”). “Contribution offering” is a better English rendering because it refers to something “taken out from” (i.e., “lifted up from”; cf. the Hebrew term הֵרִים (herim) in, e.g., Lev 2:9; 4:8, etc.) the offering as a special contribution to the specific priest who presided over the offering procedures in any particular instance (see the next verse and R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 4:335-37). Cf. TEV “as a special contribution”; NCV, NLT “as a gift.”

verses.zh: 亚伦子孙中，献平安祭牲血和脂油的，要得这右腿为分；
verses.en: The one from Aaron’s sons who presents the blood of the peace offering and fat will have the right thigh as his share,

verses.zh: 因为我从以色列人的平安祭中，取了这摇的胸和举的腿给祭司亚伦和他子孙，作他们从以色列人中所永得的分。」
verses.en: for the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution offering I have taken from the Israelites out of their peace-offering sacrifices and have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons from the people of Israel as a perpetual allotted portion.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “a perpetual regulation”; cf. NASB “as their due forever”; NRSV “as a perpetual due”; NLT “their regular share.”

verses.zh: 这是从耶和华火祭中，作亚伦受膏的分和他子孙受膏的分，正在摩西（原文是他）叫他们前来给耶和华供祭司职分的日子，
verses.en: This is the allotment of Aaron and the allotment of his sons from the Lord’s gifts on the day Moses[NOTE:1] presented them to serve as priests[NOTE:2] to the Lord.
notes: Heb “the day he”; the referent (Moses) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “in the day of he presented them to serve as priests to the Lord.” The grammar here is relatively unusual. First, the verb “presented” appears to be in the perfect rather than the infinitive (but see GKC 531), the latter being normal in such temporal expressions. Second, the active verb form appears to be used as a passive plural (“they were presented”). However, if it is translated active and singular then Moses would be the subject: “on the day he [Moses] offered them [Aaron and his sons].”

verses.zh: 就是在摩西（原文是他）膏他们的日子，耶和华吩咐以色列人给他们的。这是他们世世代代永得的分。
verses.en: This is what the Lord commanded to give to them from the Israelites on the day Moses[NOTE:1] anointed them[NOTE:2]—a perpetual allotted portion throughout their generations.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the day he”; the referent (Moses) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “which the Lord commanded to give to them in the day he anointed them from the children of Israel.” Thus v. 36 is tied syntactically to v. 35 (see the note there).
Heb “for your generations”; cf. NIV “for the generations to come”; TEV “for all time to come.”

verses.zh: 这就是燔祭、素祭、赎罪祭、赎愆祭，和平安祭的条例，并承接圣职的礼，
verses.en: This is the law[NOTE:1] for the burnt offering, the grain offering,[NOTE:2] the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering,[NOTE:3] and the peace-offering sacrifice,
notes: The Hebrew term translated “law” (תוֹרָה [torah]) occurs up to this point in the book only in Lev 6:9 [6:2 HT], 14 [7 HT], 25 [18 HT], 7:1, 7, 11, and here in 7:37. This suggests that Lev 7:37-38 is a summary of only this section of the book (i.e., Lev 6:8 [6:1 HT]-7:36), not all of Lev 1-7.
In the MT only “the grain offering” lacks a connecting ו (vav). However, many Hebrew mss, Smr, LXX, Syriac, and a ms of Tg. Onq. have the ו (vav) on “the grain offering” as well.

The inclusion of the “ordination offering” (מִלּוּאִים, milluʾim; the term apparently comes from the notion of “filling [of the hand],” cf. Lev 8:33) here anticipates Lev 8. It is a kind of peace offering, as the regulations in Lev 8:22-32 will show (cf. Exod 29:19-34). In the context of the ordination ritual for the priests it fits into the sequence of offerings as a peace offering would: sin offering (Lev 8:14-17), burnt and grain offering (Lev 8:18-21), and finally peace (i.e., ordination) offering (Lev 8:22-32). Moreover, in this case, Moses received the breast of the ordination offering as his due since he was the presiding priest over the sacrificial procedures (Lev 8:29; cf. Lev 7:30-31), while Aaron and his sons ate the portions that would have been consumed by the common worshipers in a regular peace-offering procedure (Exod 29:31-34; cf. Lev 7:15-18). For a general introduction to the peace offering see the note on Lev 3:1.

verses.zh: 都是耶和华在西奈山所吩咐摩西的，就是他在西奈旷野吩咐以色列人献供物给耶和华之日所说的。
verses.en: which the Lord commanded Moses on Mount Sinai on the day he commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the Lord in the desert of Sinai.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must
not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Exactly when the different rituals were brought together is uncertain. Surely many of them came
from the exodus period (Lev. 7:38) but others from later periods. See The Interpreters Bible, vol. 2, pp. 40-41.

- There are two different terms translated "sacrifice" that need to be distinguished.

- term used for all animal/blood offerings given to YHWH (BDB 256)

- term for the act of "slaying" the animal (BDB 1006)

Both are translated "sacrifice" in English.

- Leviticus 6-7 clarifies the information of chapters 1-5.

- wholly burnt offering ‒ 'ola (BDB 750, cf. Lev. 1:3-17; 6:8-13; 7:8)

- grain/cereal offering ‒ minha (BDB 585, cf. Lev. 2:1-16; 6:14-23; 7:9-10)

- peace offering ‒ shelem (BDB 1023, cf. Lev. 3:1-17; 7:11-34)

- sin offering ‒ hatta't (BDB 308, cf. Lev. 4:1-5:13; 6:24-30)

- guilt offering ‒ 'asam (BDB 79, cf. Lev. 5:14-6:7; 7:1-7)

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 7:1-10

1"Now this is the law of the guilt offering; it is most holy. 2In the place where they slay the burnt
offering they are to slay the guilt offering, and he shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar. 3Then
he shall offer from it all its fat: the fat tail and the fat that covers the entrails, 4and the two kidneys
with the fat that is on them, which is on the loins, and the lobe on the liver he shall remove with the kidneys.
5The priest shall offer them up in smoke on the altar as an offering by fire to the Lord;
it is a guilt offering. 6Every male among the priests may eat of it. It shall be eaten in a holy place; it is
most holy. 7The guilt offering is like the sin offering, there is one law for them; the priest who makes
atonement with it shall have it. 8Also the priest who presents any man's burnt offering, that priest
shall have for himself the skin of the burnt offering which he has presented. 9Likewise, every grain
offering that is baked in the oven and everything prepared in a pan or on a griddle shall belong to the priest who presents it.
10Every grain offering, mixed with oil or dry, shall belong to all the sons of Aaron, to all alike.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation
of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in
interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What makes an offering "most holy"?

- Why do the fat and blood belong exclusively to YHWH?

- Explain Lev. 7:18 in your own words.

- What made an animal "clean" or "unclean"?

- What does the phrase "cut off from his people" imply?

- What is the difference between a "wave offering" in Lev. 7:30 and a "wave offering" in 7:34?
